chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever performs the visitation (Ziyarah) and sleeps on the road, if he spends the night in Mecca, he is obliged to offer a sacrifice (dam); and if he has already left it, there is no obligation upon him; and if he arrives before Mina."
And that which indicates that it is preferable not to leave except after dawn is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pilgrim who sleeps on the road during Hajz and when is a sacrifice due?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific conditions for the *dam* (sacrifice) penalty when a pilgrim sleeps on the road during the *Ziyarah* phase of Hajj, distinguishing between remaining within Mecca's boundaries versus having exited or arrived prematurely at Mina. It links this legal ruling to the broader principle of timing in ritual acts, citing the preference for departing after dawn to ensure proper observance of the pilgrimage rites.
